Get ready for the annual Pumpkin Walk held on Saturday, October 17, 2026, on the grounds of the historic John Jay French Museum from 6 pm – 9 pm!

Use your creativity to decorate or carve a pumpkin and enter it into our contest. (Entry form at the bottom of this page). The fan-favorite pumpkin in several categories will be selected by ballot and prizes will be awarded, so gather your friends and family to come vote on your favorites! Prizes include, but are not limited to: TexJoy gift baskets, a Black Bear Diner giftcard, a family membership to the Houston Museum of Natural Science, and more! Float through a haunted tour of the 1845 French home featuring departed French family members, a haunted hayride of the grounds, and a Halloween craft for the kids (while supplies last). Walk through a vendor fair to check out local booths with Halloween goodies.

Admission is $5 at the gate for all non-members ages 4 and up, with kids 3 and under attending free. Beaumont Heritage Society members attend free, check your membership card for details. Beaumont Heritage Society is also participating in Museums for All, which allows free entry of groups up to 4 people with the presentation of a valid SNAP/EBT Card and a valid ID.
Want to be a vendor at this year’s Pumpkin Walk? Click here to complete your booth registration form and payment. Please note: we will not be allowing vendors to sell food at this event.

This event is part of the greater Beaumont area’s annual “Museum Madness Weekend.”  The Art Museum of Southeast Texas, Beaumont Children’s Museum, John Jay French Museum, Edison Museum, Dishman Art Museum, Fire Museum of Texas, McFaddin-Ward House Museum, Museum of the Gulf Coast, Spindletop-Gladys City Boomtown Museum, and Texas Energy Museum are each hosting events for a fun-filled weekend in Jefferson County.
Our Pumpkin Carving and Decorating Contest is FREE to enter!
Pumpkins must be dropped off at the Beaumont Heritage Society Heritage Hall Event Space (2985 French Road, Beaumont, TX, 77706) on:
All entries must be on site by Saturday, October 17th by 12 p.m.

Join us on Thursday, October 8, for an evening of soulful sounds on our beautiful grounds at Music at the McFaddins’ featuring Curse and the Cure. Gates open at 6 p.m. with music beginning at 6:30 p.m. on the McFaddin-Ward House lawn (1906 McFaddin Ave., Beaumont).

Curse and the Cure—husband and wife acoustic duo Jason and Norma Touchette—will showcase their incredible range, amazing harmonies, and dynamic vocals across a wide variety of genres and familiar hits ranging from Fleetwood Mac and the Eagles to 90s country and TLC.

The Port Neches natives have been performing together locally, nationally, and internationally since February 2014. They have opened for national and regional acts such as Reba McEntire, the Charlie Daniels Band, and Pat Green.

The concert is admission-free and open to all ages. Attendees are encouraged to bring blankets, chairs, and refreshments as they gather in the Historic Home’s gorgeous gardens to enjoy a great evening of live entertainment.
In case of inclement weather, Music at the McFaddins’ will be cancelled. For more information, call 409-832-2134.
To learn more about Curse and the Cure, visit https://curseandthecure.wordpress.com.

Music at the McFaddins’ featuring Curse and the Cure is part of Museum Madness Month 2026. This October, the Beaumont Convention and Visitors Bureau is teaming up with area museums for a full month of events and activities. Participating museums and partners include: The Art Museum of Southeast Texas, Beaumont Botanical Gardens, Beaumont Children’s Museum, Beaumont Heritage Society, Fire Museum of Texas, Jefferson County Historical Commission/Historic Magnolia Cemetery, McFaddin-Ward House Museum, Spindletop Boomtown Museum, Temple to the Brave, Texas Energy Museum, and Tyrrell Park Nature Center.

Join the McFaddin-Ward House Museum for “The Texas Sports Revolution: How the Lone Star State Changed the Culture of American Athletics,” a free public lecture presented by Frank A. Guridy on Thursday, October 15, at 6:30 p.m. in the Museum’s Visitor Center Lecture Hall (1906 Calder Avenue, Beaumont).

Award-winning historian and author Frank A. Guridy will explore how the United States became a sports-crazed nation during the 1960s and 70s, emphasizing the decisive role Texas-based athletes and sports entrepreneurs played in the country’s dramatic transformation.

Guridy is an accomplished scholar whose research has focused on sport history, urban history, and the history of American social movements. Currently, he serves as a professor of history at Columbia University in New York City.

He is the author of numerous scholarly works on the intersection of sports, society, and politics, including the books The Stadium: An American History of Politics, Protest, and Play (2024) and The Sports Revolution: How Texas Changed the Culture of American Athletics (2021), and has provided commentary on a wide variety of podcasts, radio, and TV programs.
McFaddin-Ward House Museum lectures are admission-free and open to the public, but space is limited. Doors open at 6 p.m. For more information, call 409-832-2134.

For those unable to attend, the full lecture will be available for viewing on the Museum YouTube Channel (youtube.com/@mcfaddinwardhouse), Facebook (facebook.com/McFaddinWardHouse), and website (mcfaddin-ward.org/about/videos) after the event.

This event is part of Museum Madness Month 2026. During October, the Beaumont Convention and Visitors Bureau is teaming up with area museums for a full month of events and activities. Participating museums and partners include: The Art Museum of Southeast Texas, Beaumont Botanical Gardens, Beaumont Children’s Museum, Beaumont Heritage Society, Fire Museum of Texas, Jefferson County Historical Commission/Historic Magnolia Cemetery, McFaddin-Ward House Museum, Spindletop Boomtown Museum, Temple to the Brave, Texas Energy Museum, and Tyrrell Park Nature Center.

Join us on Thursday, November 5 for an evening of fantastic sounds on our beautiful grounds at Music at the McFaddins’ featuring Jimmy Simmons &
column3: Friends. Gates open at 6 p.m. with music beginning at 6:30 p.m. on the McFaddin-Ward House east lawn (1906 McFaddin Ave., Beaumont).

column1: Simmons and his band will perform a varied mix of classics from the big band era through modern day hits.

President Emeritus of Lamar University and a member of the faculty and leadership team for more than four decades, Simmons is an accomplished musician with an active performance career. He has played alongside an impressive list of famous musicians such as Frank Sinatra, Ray Charles, Bob Hope, Jerry Lewis, Chicago, and The Temptations.

The concert is admission-free and open to all ages. Attendees are encouraged to bring blankets, chairs, and refreshments as they gather in the Historic Home’s gorgeous gardens to enjoy a great evening of live entertainment.
In case of inclement weather, Music at the McFaddins’ will be cancelled. For more information, call 409-832-2134.

**Rescheduled from the Nov. 19 performance with The Golden Triangle Big Band, which has been cancelled due to an unforeseen scheduling conflict.

Join us for the annual McFaddin-Ward House Museum Holiday Photo Shoot on Sunday, November 8, from 12 p.m. – 2 p.m. This family friendly opportunity is admission-free!

Photos will be taken inside the Historic Home in the Entrance Hall, with the stunning grand staircase beautifully draped in festive décor as your backdrop. A staff photographer will take up to three photos of each group or individual using your personal device (digital camera or cell phone).

Join the McFaddin-Ward House Museum for “America 250: A Beaumont History,” a free public lecture presented by Judith Walker Linsley on Thursday, November 12, at 6:30 p.m. in the Museum’s Visitor Center Lecture Hall (1906 Calder Avenue, Beaumont).

In commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary, Linsley, a sixth-generation Southeast Texan and local historian, will explore the fascinating story of Beaumont, beginning with the Indigenous Ishak people and traveling through the Texas Revolution, the 1901 Spindletop oil boom, and technological and industrial expansions leading up to the modern day.

For nearly four decades, Linsley has been a member of the McFaddin-Ward House Museum staff, serving in a range of roles in interpretation, education, curation, and research, including her current role as research assistant. She has also conducted more than 100 oral history interviews for the Museum.

A Lamar University alumna with a Bachelor of Arts in Spanish and a Master of Arts in History, Linsley served as the second director of Lamar’s Center for History and Culture of Southeast Texas and the Upper Gulf Coast and has been an adjunct instructor of both Texas and U.S. history at Lamar.

She has co-authored three books, including the award-winning Giant Under the Hill: A History of the Spindletop Oil Discovery at Beaumont, Texas, in 1901 (2002) and The McFaddin-Ward House (1992), and numerous historical articles.
McFaddin-Ward House Museum lectures are admission-free and open to the public, but space is limited. Doors open at 6 p.m. For more information, call 409-832-2134.

For those unable to attend, the full lecture will be available for viewing on the Museum YouTube Channel (youtube.com/@mcfaddinwardhouse), Facebook (facebook.com/McFaddinWardHouse), and website (mcfaddin-ward.org/about/videos) after the event.

The lecture is part of Southeast Texas 250, a regional initiative to commemorate the U.S. Semiquincentennial celebration. Led by the Beaumont Heritage Society, Southeast Texas 250 brings together museums, historical organizations, schools, civic groups, and local governments throughout the region to celebrate the people, places, and stories that have shaped Southeast Texas and its role in the broader American story.

The McFaddin-Ward House invites the community to delight in the splendor, sounds, and spirit of the season at its annual admission-free Holiday Open House Weekend on Saturday, Dec. 5, and Sunday, Dec. 6, from 5-7 p.m.

column1: Guests will enjoy festive refreshments, live music, carolers, and Santa’s Craft Workshop with children’s activities at the museum’s Visitor Center (1906 Calder Avenue in Beaumont) before making their way across the street to see the historic house shining with holiday cheer and twinkling lights. New this year, guests of all ages are invited to embark on a merry ride around the grounds aboard a trackless train, adding to the fun.

Inside the home, visitors will tour a visual wonderland of magnificent holiday décor throughout the first floor, while traditional Christmas music plays on the Music Room’s grand piano. This year’s holiday interpretation will allow guests to experience a McFaddin family open house party. Gorgeous gold, shining silver, and sparkling crystal light up the dining areas, while glamorous party clothes and other special items, like a vintage toy train, will be on display. Before departing, guests will have the opportunity to take photos with Santa on the front porch to complete the magic memories of the evening.

The event is admission-free and open to all ages. For more information, call 409-832-2134.

The McFaddin-Ward House Education Department will offer “Christmas Past,” a free Homeschool Workshop for ages 8 – 12, on Tuesday, December 15, from 10 to 11:30 a.m. in the Museum’s Visitor Center Lecture Hall (1906 Calder Avenue, Beaumont).

The holiday has seen many changes through the decades. Students will take a look back at what Christmas was like from 1900 – 1950. Participants will also enjoy a walk-through tour of the first floor of the historic home magnificently decorated for the holiday season.
Registration is not required, but seating is limited.

**Please note: This is not a drop off event. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

column2: >The McFaddin-Ward House Museum invites the community to its fifth annual SOAR Family Day on Sunday, March 7, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. on the Museum’s grounds (1906 McFaddin Ave., Beaumont).

>The admission-free, family-friendly event will feature a full afternoon of butterfly-related activities, including garden and butterfly related crafts, local artist Butterfly Art Garden display, butterfly ride-on bikes, butterfly performance artists, and booths from community partners and exhibitors. >In case of inclement weather, SOAR Family Day will be cancelled.

Look for graceful herons, turtles, fish, and even an occasional alligator on the banks.

Join Rhythm of Our Roots, a free intergenerational community gathering presented by The Healing Portal Collective that transforms the park into a space for wellness, creativity, and connection. Experience guided Meridian Movement with Dr. Charlie Trinh, exploring gentle stretching, breathwork, and mindful movement inspired by Traditional Chinese Medicine. Relax into a restorative crystal bowl sound journey led by
column2: utm_source=qr"">Blossom Legend, then join our signature community drum circle facilitated by Meesh Martinez, where rhythm becomes a shared language that brings people together.

column1: Designed for all ages and experience levels, this gathering offers accessible practices that support emotional well-being, self-expression, and community connection. Come as you are and rediscover the rhythm that connects us all.
Presented as part of Buffalo Bayou Partnership’
column2: s Park Partners program, an initiative that connects neighborhood organizations with opportunities to activate parks, trails, and unique spaces along Buffalo Bayou.

column1: Dr. Charlie Trinh / Trinhquility is a Doctor of Acupuncture and Chinese Medicine, holistic healer, and community wellness advocate based in Houston. With a unique background in engineering and a deep-rooted calling toward Eastern medicine, Dr. Trinh integrates Traditional Chinese Medicine, movement practices, and energetic healing to support the body’
column2: s natural ability to restore balance. His work bridges ancient wisdom with modern understanding, emphasizing the connection between physical health, emotional well-being, and the surrounding environment. Through his practice, Trinhquility, Dr. Trinh has developed Meridian Movements, a mindful movement system designed to activate the body&#8217
column3: s energetic pathways, improve circulation, and reconnect individuals to their natural rhythms. His vision for the Bayou project is to bring accessible, community-centered healing into nature, creating spaces where individuals can engage in intentional movement, breath, and awareness alongside the living ecosystem. By aligning human health with environmental harmony, Dr. Trinh aims to foster resilience, connection, and collective well-being within the Houston community.

column1: Meesh Martinez / Primitive Experience is a multimedia producer, filmmaker, and community arts facilitator based in Houston, Texas. An Austin native who grew up in Mexico City, Meesh holds a Bachelor’
column2: s degree in Cinematographic Language, a background that informs his work in visual storytelling, cultural documentation, and multimedia production. In Houston, Meesh collaborates with artists, organizations, and cultural institutions to produce video, photography, and digital media that document performances, community initiatives, and creative projects. His work focuses on amplifying cultural expression and strengthening connections between artists and communities. Meesh is also the founder of Primitive Experience, an initiative that creates immersive gatherings through drum circles, music, movement, and nature-based practices designed to foster connection, creativity, and collective well-being. Meesh is certified in facilitating drum circles for emotional regulation, using rhythm and group participation as tools for personal and community healing. In addition to his artistic and multimedia work, Meesh contributes to youth development programs and will be participating in the leadership and direction team for Peace Camp, supporting programming that nurtures creativity, emotional awareness, and community values for young participants. Meesh is also currently leading projects supported through grant funding that expand access to participatory arts experiences and cultural programming in Houston.

utm_source=qr"">Goddess Glow Birthing is a full-spectrum community doula, herbalist, chef, musician, and wellness facilitator dedicated to creating experiences that nourish the body, mind, and spirit. With more than a decade of experience in community wellness, culinary arts, and holistic care, her work weaves together ancestral wisdom, cultural traditions, nourishment, sound, and collective healing. Rooted in Afro-Caribbean traditions and a deep commitment to community care, Blossom creates spaces where people can slow down, reconnect with themselves, and experience healing in ways that are both accessible and transformative. As a chef of over twelve years, Blossom believes food is one of our most powerful medicines and a pathway to connection. Her culinary work focuses on nourishing meals, herbal preparations, botanical beverages, and community-centered dining experiences that celebrate the relationship between wellness, culture, and the earth. As an herbalist and doula, she supports individuals and families through life’
column3:
s transitions, offering holistic care that honors the physical, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of well-being. At Rhythm of Our Roots, Blossom will guide a restorative sound bath experience designed to help participants release stress, regulate the nervous system, and reconnect with their own inner rhythm. Using healing vibrations, frequency harmonics, and meditative soundscapes, she invites participants into a state of deep rest, reflection, and renewal. Her approach is grounded in the belief that personal healing ripples outward, strengthening families, communities, and future generations.

Volunteers, ages 9 and up, are invited to join Buffalo Bayou Partnership and Leave No Trace for a family-friendly fun volunteer day. Volunteer activity and meeting location will be determined and emailed the day before the volunteer project.
Please reach out to volunteer@buffalobayou.org if you’re interested in signing up a group of 10 or more individuals.

Leave No Trace is a supporter-based nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting the outdoors through science-based education that inspires responsible recreation. As more people visit parks, trails, and public lands, the pressure on our natural spaces grows. Leave No Trace works to ensure that everyone—no matter where they explore—has the knowledge and tools to enjoy nature while minimizing their impact.

Learn about native plants and the insects that pollinate them along Buffalo Bayou! Follow along this discovery tour of Houston’s historic waterway ecosystem with Nancy Greig, founding director of the Cockrell Butterfly Center (now retired). An avid natural historian “jack of all trades”, she has particular interest in plants and insects, but birds, mammals, herpetofauna, and fish are all on her radar. At home she keeps busy with a butterfly garden, honey bee hives, and purple martin houses.
Joining this month’s walk are special guests from Leave No Trace, who will be incorporating education about Leave No Trace principles into this nature walk.
The Water Works in Buffalo Bayou Park (105-B Sabine St)

Leave No Trace is a supporter-based nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting the outdoors through science-based education that inspires responsible recreation. As more people visit parks, trails, and public lands, the pressure on our natural spaces grows. Leave No Trace works to ensure that everyone—no matter where they explore—has the knowledge and tools to enjoy nature while minimizing their impact.

Enjoy an evening of poetry and immersive art, presented in conjunction with Undercurrents by Rafael Lozano-Hemmer in the Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern. The night begins with a poetry reading by one of the acclaimed writers who contributed to the installation and drinks on the terrace. Then, descend into the Cistern for a unique opportunity to experience Undercurrents with the writers.
The reading begins on the Wortham Insurance Terrace above the Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern. (105-B Sabine St)

Roberto Tejada is the author of poetry collections that include Mirrors for Gold (Krupskaya, 2006), Exposition Park (Wesleyan, 2010), Why the Assembly Disbanded (Fordham, 2022), and Carbonate of Copper (Fordham, 2025), longlisted for the PEN/Jean Stein Book Award. His writings on art and media history include National Camera: Photography and Mexico’s Image Environment (Minnesota, 2009), his work on the groundbreaking Mexican American artist Celia Alvarez Muñoz (UCLA/CSRC
column2:
Minnesota, 2009) and essay collections on Latin American and Latinx art and culture Still Nowhere in an Empty Vastness (Noemi, 2019), and the forthcoming Along the Diagonal: Art / Essays / América (Fordham, 2026). Awarded a John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation Fellowship in Poetry (2021) he is the Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen Distinguished Professor at the University of Houston where he teaches Creative Writing and Art History.

column1: Join Buffalo Bayou Partnership and Texas Children in Nature for a free outdoor screening of Deep in the Heart 2: Texas Rivers, a newly released film celebrating the waterways that sustain Texas wildlife, communities, and ecosystems.

The second film in the much-acclaimed Deep in the Heart series, Texas Rivers takes you on a beautiful journey across the state, with stunning scenery and plenty of adorable river residents along the way.
Bring your blankets, lawn chairs, and the whole family, and settle in for an evening under the stars. Food trucks, drinks, and popcorn available for purchase.
The Water Works in Buffalo Bayou Park (105-B Sabine St)

Step into a deeper stillness inside the spacious and tranquil Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern.

Offered in collaboration with UNIONisCREATION™, this meditation and sound experience invites guests into a space of resonance, restoration, and inner alignment. Through gentle vibrations of singing bowls, wind chimes, and a gong, along with guided awareness, participants are supported in reconnecting body and mind.

column2: it is a practice of listening, feeling, and returning to center within one of Houston&#8217
column3: s most iconic, immersive spaces. Each session unfolds as a shared moment of reflection, connection, and sound-guided stillness.

column1: Guests should bring their own cushions or mats. No food or drinks are allowed inside the Cistern.

Buffalo Bayou Partnership (BBP) is making progress on trails, parks, and unique spaces east of downtown!

Join us at the iconic Warehouse at Turkey Bend for our annual presentation sharing progress, important milestones in design and construction, and exciting changes to come as we realize the Buffalo Bayou East 10-Year Plan.

The event will begin with presentations and a panel discussion with members of the architecture and landscape architecture design teams working on BBP projects, followed by a reception and after-party with refreshments and music.
¡Buffalo Bayou Partnership (BBP) está avanzando en la construcción de senderos, parques y espacios únicos al este del centro de la ciudad!

Acompáñanos en el icónico Warehouse at Turkey Bend para nuestra presentación anual, donde compartiremos los avances, hitos importantes en el diseño y la construcción, y los emocionantes cambios que están por venir mientras hacemos realidad el Plan de 10 Años de Buffalo Bayou East.

El evento comenzará con presentaciones y un panel de discusión con integrantes de los equipos de arquitectura y arquitectura paisajista que trabajan en los proyectos de BBP. Después, disfrutaremos de una recepción y fiesta con bebidas y música.

Step into a deeper stillness inside the spacious and tranquil Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern.

Offered in collaboration with UNIONisCREATION™, this meditation and sound experience invites guests into a space of resonance, restoration, and inner alignment. Through gentle vibrations of singing bowls, wind chimes, and a gong, along with guided awareness, participants are supported in reconnecting body and mind.

column2: it is a practice of listening, feeling, and returning to center within one of Houston&#8217
column3: s most iconic, immersive spaces. Each session unfolds as a shared moment of reflection, connection, and sound-guided stillness.

column1: Guests should bring their own cushions or mats. No food or drinks are allowed inside the Cistern.
